overview.body:
Founded by brothers Michal and Lukasz Wywrot, LCH grew from investing in and building homes into a developer and development manager. Every role on our team today is one the founders once did themselves, and that still shapes how we work: lean, hands-on and accountable for results.

We develop our own purpose-built rental communities and manage development and construction for owners, institutions, lenders and receivers, with construction management through our affiliate, Elevate.

We also own and operate Merge Spaces, the coworking and community hub on Kingston Road where our own office is based, which gives us day-to-day experience as an operator, not only as a builder.
overview.imageAlt: LCH founders Michal and Lukasz Wywrot with a model of Everston

values.title: Purpose
values.body: We aim to create lasting value through homes and places that work for residents, partners and their surroundings.

values.title: Transparency
values.body: Clear reporting, open conversations and visible responsibilities support informed decisions throughout a project.

values.title: Efficiency
values.body: Early planning and coordinated decisions help the team manage cost, schedule and the work required for delivery.

timeline.title: Lifestyle Custom Homes
timeline.text: LCH began as Lifestyle Custom Homes, building precision custom homes. That hands-on experience in design, procurement and site delivery shaped the kind of development we wanted to do next: well-built communities at higher density.

timeline.title: One6Nine Jones and St. Leslieville completed
timeline.text: Twelve new townhomes and 14 lofts in a restored 1913 church, side by side on Jones Avenue, showed the growing range of the business.

timeline.title: Into mid-rise with Merge Condos
timeline.text: LCH moved into mid-rise development with Merge Condos, where Kingston Road meets Danforth Avenue. With final planning approvals in place, condominium sales launched in 2019 and construction followed in 2020.

images.alt: Merge Condos rendering from the 2019 launch
images.caption: Rendering

timeline.title: Merge Spaces
timeline.text: LCH opened Merge Spaces, a coworking and community hub on Kingston Road that we own and operate and that also houses our own office. Elevate managed preconstruction and construction.

timeline.title: Merge Condos completed
timeline.text: Merge marked a step in the company’s growth, carrying a larger condominium development through approvals, construction, occupancy and closeout.

images.alt: Completed Merge Condos at Kingston Road and Danforth Avenue

timeline.title: Jefferson Heights
timeline.text: For receiver Albert Gelman, with Cameron Stephens, LCH and Elevate took on a partially completed townhome development in Richmond Hill, re-establishing budget and schedule control and advancing it toward occupancy and closings.

images.alt: Townhomes at Jefferson Heights in Richmond Hill

timeline.title: Everston breaks ground
timeline.text: Construction began on Phase 1 of Everston, 358 of its 566 purpose-built rental homes in West Hill, with Elevate managing construction. Both tower cranes were up by October.

images.alt: Everston’s tower cranes during construction, October 2025

timeline.title: Cliffside breaks ground
timeline.text: Construction began on Cliffside, now 209 purpose-built rental homes in Cliffside Village, while Everston topped off and opened pre-leasing.

images.alt: Tower crane and excavation at Cliffside

timeline.title: Eaglebay Towns
timeline.text: For KPMG and RBC, LCH and Elevate stepped in on a 29-home townhouse receivership in Newcastle, combining construction completion with purchaser, warranty and closeout coordination.

timeline.label: 2027 and beyond
timeline.title: A growing rental portfolio
timeline.text: Everston prepares to welcome its first residents and Cliffside continues to rise. Retreat, with Fiera Real Estate, and 415 Broadview, with its heritage church, are the next communities to move forward.

images.alt: Proposed new building alongside the retained church at 415 Broadview
images.caption: Rendering

expertise.heading: What we bring to a project.

items.title: Feasibility and development strategy
items.body: Site and market review, massing and unit-mix testing, development budgets, pro formas, cash flow and schedules that show what a project can achieve, whether it is a new site or an existing scheme that needs rethinking.

items.title: Planning, approvals and permits
items.body: Municipal strategy and the full approvals path: rezonings, official plan amendments, site plan approval, minor variances, building permits, municipal agreements and clearances, with consultants and agencies coordinated throughout.

items.title: Design management and optimization
items.body: Floorplates, unit mix, parking, building systems and suite and amenity design are tested together against rentable area, construction cost and long-term operation, then turned into clear direction for the design team.

items.title: Budgets, financing support and reporting
items.body: Development budgets, cost-to-complete tracking, risk registers, decision logs and owner reporting, plus support with lenders, CMHC and affordable-housing programs.

items.title: Construction management through Elevate
items.body: Preconstruction, estimating and virtual builds, tendering and procurement, then site management, safety, quality, schedule control, turnover and warranty.

items.title: Project recovery and receiverships
items.body: Stabilizing partially completed projects, reviewing deficiencies and documentation, re-pricing the remaining work, and managing occupancy, registration, purchaser and closing requirements.

items.title: Jefferson Heights
items.heading: Bringing an incomplete project toward delivery.
items.body: At Jefferson Heights in Richmond Hill, LCH and Elevate worked on a partially completed residential development for receiver Albert Gelman, with Cameron Stephens. The assignment brought together development management and construction delivery: re-establishing budget and schedule control, coordinating consultants and trades, and advancing occupancy, registration, sales and closing requirements.
items.imageAlt: Townhomes at Jefferson Heights in Richmond Hill

items.title: Eaglebay Towns
items.heading: Coordinating construction and closeout.
items.body: For KPMG and RBC, LCH and Elevate were engaged on a 29-home townhouse receivership in Newcastle, Clarington. The mandate combined construction stabilization and completion with coordination of purchaser, warranty and closeout requirements.

items.title: 150 The Donway West
items.heading: An in-depth development report.
items.body: For Akelius, LCH and Elevate prepared an in-depth development report on new rental housing beside occupied buildings, covering the market, design and construction refinements, costing, financial modelling and an approvals strategy.
items.imageAlt: Aerial rendering of new rental buildings beside existing apartments at 150 The Donway West

items.title: 5122 Timberlea
items.heading: Taking an industrial expansion through approvals.
items.body: For the owner of an operating industrial facility in Mississauga, LCH managed the planning approvals for an expansion, securing the Minor Variance and taking the project through Site Plan Approval.
items.imageAlt: 3D massing view of the proposed warehouse addition at 5122 Timberlea Boulevard

lchElevate.heading: Two companies, one team.
lchElevate.intro: Affiliated companies with their own teams and clients. On our projects they work as one: LCH carries the development and the owner’s interests, while Elevate plans and builds, so cost, schedule and buildability are settled early.
